_README: Food content. Dish/experience names & descriptions are editorial (real). No invented prices or class durations — those vary by operator and are shown as 'check when you book'.

eat.d: Samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi grilled at your table, wrapped in lettuce with ssamjang and garlic.
Chewy rice cakes in sweet-spicy sauce, plus hotteok, gimbap and fish cakes from market stalls.
Rice bowl topped with vegetables, egg and gochujang — mix it all together before eating.
Extra-crispy fried chicken with beer — 'chimaek' is a national pastime.
Chewy buckwheat noodles in icy broth — a refreshing summer favorite.
Certified halal spots cluster around Itaewon; temple-food and veggie options are growing citywide.
Specialty coffee and creative desserts in Seoul's trendiest cafe district.
Bubbling stews like kimchi-jjigae and budae-jjigae — hearty and cheap.
A whole young chicken stuffed with rice, ginseng and garlic in a milky broth — a restorative summer classic.
A hearty, spicy pork-spine and potato stew simmered with perilla and greens — a late-night comfort favourite.
Busan’s signature pork-and-rice soup — a warming bowl of broth, pork and rice you season to taste.
Andong-style braised chicken with glass noodles, potatoes and vegetables in a savoury-sweet soy sauce.
A griddled street pancake filled with molten brown sugar, cinnamon and nuts — best in winter.
Chewy sweet-potato glass noodles stir-fried with vegetables and a touch of sesame — a party staple.
Korean blood sausage stuffed with noodles and barley — a market and pojangmacha staple, often served with tteokbokki.
Hand-cut wheat noodles in a warming broth of anchovy, chicken or clam — simple, comforting home cooking.
Tender boiled pork, sliced and wrapped in cabbage with salted shrimp, garlic and fresh kimchi.
Fresh raw fish, Korean-style and best by the coast — served with chogochujang or as a chilled mulhoe soup.
Seaweed rice rolls packed with vegetables, egg and more — the cheap, portable classic for a quick meal or picnic.
Chicken, cabbage and rice cakes stir-fried in a sweet-spicy sauce on a hot plate — the cheese-topped version is a favourite. A Chuncheon speciality, great for sharing.
A bubbling, spicy stew of silky uncurdled tofu with seafood or pork, served with rice and often a raw egg cracked in at the table.
A hearty hot-pot of kimchi, sausage, ham, instant noodles and cheese in a spicy broth — a post-war invention that is now comfort food for groups.
Raw crab marinated in soy sauce until silky and briny — nicknamed the 'rice thief' because it is so good with rice. An adventurous local favourite.
A crisp scallion pancake, often loaded with seafood (haemul-pajeon). Koreans love it with makgeolli rice wine, especially on a rainy day.
A mountain of fine shaved ice topped with sweet red beans (patbingsu), fruit, condensed milk or matcha — the go-to summer dessert to share.
Korean dumplings stuffed with pork, tofu and vegetables — steamed, pan-fried, or dropped into soup as mandu-guk.
Pig's trotters slow-braised in soy and spices until tender, sliced and eaten with salted-shrimp sauce and lettuce wraps.
Silky hand-cut raw beef seasoned with sesame oil and pear, often topped with an egg yolk — Korea's take on tartare.
A milky ox-bone broth simmered for hours, served with rice and noodles — you season it yourself with salt and spring onion.
Chilled noodles in a cool, nutty soybean broth — a refreshing summer dish, usually eaten with a pinch of salt.
Beef or pork intestines grilled at the table until crisp and smoky — a rich, much-loved dish to share over drinks.

make.d: Make and pack your own kimchi to take home; classes typically run with an English guide.
Cook a full Korean meal from scratch with a chef, then eat what you made.
Shape colorful traditional rice cakes — family-friendly and hands-on.
Learn to brew and taste Korean rice wine, usually with pairing snacks.

tips: A restaurant full of locals is usually a good sign.
Many places have picture menus or English menus; convenience stores are great for cheap late-night eats.
Side dishes (banchan) are free and often refillable.
For halal food, the Itaewon area has the most certified options.
Class prices and durations vary by operator — check the details when you book.
